section_summary: Most of this section consists of January 1947 declarations by Swiss banks identifying Japanese dollar bonds and their owners for submission through the Swiss Legation. Later documents discuss private financing of Japanese imports, protection of foreign investments during the occupation, liquidation of the Bank of Taiwan, and proposed reforms to Japanese public finance. The section ends with a second, incomplete copy of the public finance policy paper.

subfiles.summary: Says 64 declarations were forwarded to SCAP and government securities can receive the same treatment.

subfiles.title: Bogdan proposal for private financing of Japanese imports
subfiles.about: Proposes a bank syndicate credit to finance Japanese imports and repay lenders from exports.
subfiles.summary: Bogdan suggests a $20–25 million credit for cotton and other imports, initially limited to short maturities. He proposes a cash margin, liens on goods and export proceeds, and War Department assurance against extraordinary disruptions.

subfiles.title: Address and filing sheet for Bogdan letter
subfiles.about: Identifies the sender and recipient of Bogdan's April 9 letter.
subfiles.summary: Address sheet for the preceding letter.

subfiles.title: Bogdan wool processing and barter proposal
subfiles.about: Presents a private wool shipment, processing, and possible barter arrangement with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Bogdan describes Hart Inc.'s proposal to send raw wool to Japan for conversion into yarn, with Japanese costs paid in wool. He also mentions exchanging wool for raw silk.

subfiles.title: Martin reply on private financing of Japanese trade
subfiles.about: Sets out State Department principles for private credit supporting Japanese imports and exports.
subfiles.summary: Martin favors initial loans for materials used in export production, with repayment from resulting exports. He also urges flexible currencies and markets, safeguards for lenders, and eventual repayment from general export proceeds.

subfiles.title: Protection of Allied shareholdings and debentures in Japanese concerns
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP procedures for protecting United Nations nationals' investments in Japanese companies.
subfiles.summary: The despatch quotes the Civil Property Custodian on preservation orders, approval requirements for transactions, investigation of unidentified property, and protection during reorganization or liquidation. It lists three enclosures.

subfiles.title: Protection of foreign property interests
subfiles.to: Economic and Scientific Section, Anti-Trust and Cartels
subfiles.about: Requests procedures to protect foreign-owned securities and other property during holding-company liquidation.
subfiles.summary: Proposes ownership investigations, separate custody, cash reserves for proceeds, and special handling of patents and machinery.

subfiles.title: Protection of United Nations nationals in Japanese industry reorganization
subfiles.about: Requests preservation of Allied nationals' stock control and related rights during corporate reorganization.
subfiles.summary: Calls for restitution safeguards and Civil Property Custodian review of reorganization plans.

subfiles.title: Holding Company Liquidation Commission report
subfiles.about: Reports steps taken to identify and protect securities and other assets formerly owned by foreigners.
subfiles.summary: The commission describes separate custody, reserve and income funds, ownership investigations, and instructions to holding companies. Chairman T. Sasayama signs the report.

subfiles.title: CINCFE telegram on reparations and the 1948 budget
subfiles.about: Reports reparations committee decisions and asks for personnel and budget information.
subfiles.summary: Discusses machine tools, advance transfers, delayed arrivals, the 1948 budget, and Kane's status.

subfiles.title: SCAP telegram on Bank of Taiwan liquidation
subfiles.to: Department of State, attention Edwin M. Martin
subfiles.about: Seeks authority to liquidate Japanese branches of the Bank of Taiwan without waiting for home-office claims.
subfiles.summary: SCAP argues that delay harms Japanese depositors and proposes leaving the home-office balance for a final settlement involving Taiwan or China.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum for proposed Japanese public finance policy
subfiles.about: Forwards the State Department's proposed Japanese public finance policy for committee consideration.
subfiles.summary: Requests referral to the Far East subcommittee.

subfiles.title: Duplicate CINCFE reparations telegram
subfiles.about: Repeats the telegram on reparations machine tools, personnel, the 1948 budget, and Kane.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of page 299.

subfiles.title: Proposed policy statement on Japanese public finance, partial copy
subfiles.about: Recommends legislative control, public debt reform, and progressive taxation in occupied Japan.
subfiles.summary: The text begins mid-paragraph and calls for transparent budgets, legislative oversight, and limits on subsidies. It recommends broad distribution of government debt, reduced inflationary financing, progressive income and estate taxes, and better enforcement. Recommendations and appendices explain the policy's occupation and deconcentration aims.

subfiles.title: Japanese public finance policy statement, second copy
subfiles.about: Presents another copy of the proposed Japanese public finance policy statement.
subfiles.summary: This copy begins with the policy question and repeats recommendations for legislative control of budgets, limits on subsidies, wider bond ownership, and progressive taxation. Its appendices discuss democratic oversight, demilitarization, and public debt. The copy continues beyond page 320.
